mainTopic: How documents are dated (tied documents and a ruler's titles), Greek number-words in two ברייתות, and stories and teachings about לשון הרע.
overview: The amud opens with רבי's challenge to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, who allowed a שטר מקושר to be opened and used as a שטר פשוט. A tied document counts the king's years one ahead, so opening it makes it look a year later. A creditor could use this to claim an already-repaid loan is a new one. The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds אין כותבין שובר, so that trick cannot happen. It also explains that רבי learned this dating custom from זונין. Next comes a document dated 'the year of so-and-so ארכן'. The גמרא shows that ארכן is the title for a ruler's first year, so we check when he took office. Because the Greek word דיגון came up, the גמרא brings two ברייתות that use Greek number-words: one about a נזיר vow and one teaching that only a four-walled house can get נגעים, learned from the word 'walls' appearing twice. The amud ends with stories about רבי's son naming the writer of a document and a ספר תהלים. They teach that even praise can lead to לשון הרע. Then comes רב's teaching that no one escapes three sins each day, and the גמרא's surprise about לשון הרע, which is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: The two documents are dated differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי objects to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: a שטר מקושר and a שטר פשוט count the king's years differently, so you can't simply turn one into the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the date of this kind of document is not the same as the date of that kind! In an ordinary document, if the king has reigned one year, we count one year, and if two, we count two. In a tied document, if the king has reigned one year, we count two, and if two, we count three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי is attacking the idea that a tied document can be opened up and used as an ordinary one. He points out that the two types are dated in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר מקושר adds one extra year to the king's reign. If you open it up and read it as a שטר פשוט, the date now looks one year later than the real date of the loan. So the document is effectively postdated, and the next steps show why that is dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so... (opens a challenge)
An ordinary, flat document signed at the bottom
A tied document, folded and stitched, with witnesses signing on the back of each fold
They count (the years of the king's reign)

steps.confusionAlert: The extra year is not a mistake. It is the normal dating custom for tied documents. The problem only comes up when someone reads a tied document as if it were an ordinary one.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה זְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל זֶה
phrases.english: But is not the date of this one unlike
phrases.notes: רבי is pushing back on רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, who said a tied document can be made into an ordinary one.

phrases.english: the date of that one!

phrases.aramaic: פָּשׁוּט; מָלַךְ שָׁנָה – מוֹנִין לוֹ שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: An ordinary one: if he reigned one year, they count one year for him,
two, they count two for him.

phrases.aramaic: מְקוּשָּׁר; מָלַךְ שָׁנָה – מוֹנִין לוֹ שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: A tied one: if he reigned one year, they count two for him,
two, they count three for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה זְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל זֶה לִזְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens רבי's challenge to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's ruling, which was stated just before this text.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's claim that a tied document signed inside is valid because it can be made into an ordinary one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tied documents count one extra year. Opening one up as an ordinary document makes it look postdated by a year.

steps.title: The early repayment and the receipt
steps.stepSummary: רבי describes a case: the debtor pays back a tied-document loan early, the creditor says he lost the note, and he writes a receipt instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes a person borrows money with a tied document, and he happens to get money in the meantime and pays the lender back. He says: Give me my document. The lender says: I lost it. So the lender writes him a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי continues his challenge by setting up a real-life case. This step is the setup, and the next step shows the trick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debtor pays before the due date and gets a שובר instead of the original note. The receipt is dated normally, with the real year. The tied note is still out there with its extra year built in.

phrases.english: And sometimes he borrows money from him with a tied document,
and money happens to come his way in the meantime,
and he repays him;
and he says to him: Give me my document,
and he says to him: I lost it;
and he writes him a receipt;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a concrete case on the dating difference from step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a case where the dating gap can be used to cheat the debtor.

steps.title: The creditor's trick
steps.stepSummary: When the due date comes, the creditor opens the tied note into an ordinary one and claims it is a new loan, made after the receipt.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the due date arrives, the lender turns the document into an ordinary one and says to him: This is a loan you took from me just now!
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבי's challenge by showing the actual danger. The creditor uses the extra year to make the old, already-paid loan look like a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once opened, the note reads as if it were dated a year later, which is after the receipt. The creditor can say the receipt was for some earlier loan and this note is a later one. So the debtor would pay twice. That is why רבי says a tied document should not be turned into an ordinary one.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי's concern: opening a tied document makes it look a year later, so a creditor could claim a repaid loan is a new loan dated after the receipt.

phrases.english: and when its due date arrives,
he makes it into an ordinary document,
and says to him:
These you borrowed from me just now!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָטֵי זִמְנֵיהּ מְשַׁוֵּי לֵיהּ פָּשׁוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the case begun in step 2 by showing how the creditor uses it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's ruling that the tied document can be made ordinary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The postdated look of the opened document lets the creditor claim the loan came after the receipt and collect twice.

steps.title: We do not write receipts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds אין כותבין שובר, so the receipt scenario never happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: we do not write a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חנינא בן גמליאל by removing the receipt from the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, a creditor who lost his note cannot settle the debt with a receipt. The debtor does not have to pay until the note itself is returned. Since the note is handed back when the loan is paid, the creditor never has it later to open and misuse, so רבי's trick cannot work.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not write a receipt to settle a debt

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the rule about tied documents to the separate debate over whether a debt can be settled with a שובר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל can allow opening a tied document because he holds אין כותבין שובר: the debt is paid only when the note is returned.

phrases.english: He holds: One does not write a receipt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's challenge from steps 1-3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the premise: the receipt in רבי's case is never written in this view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Opening a tied document lets a creditor cheat a debtor who holds only a receipt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since no receipts are written, the debtor always gets the note back, so the danger does not exist.

steps.title: Did רבי really know the dating rules of a tied document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי's earlier objection with a story where רבי himself did not know how a שטר מקושר is dated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was רבי really an expert in tied documents? There was a tied document brought to רבי, and he said: 'This document is postdated!' Then זונין told him: 'That is the custom of this nation. When the king has ruled one year, they count it as two. When he has ruled two, they count it as three.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי could object (back in step 1) using the special way a שטר מקושר counts the king's years, when a story shows he once didn't know that custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1, רבי's objection depended on knowing that tied documents count the king's years one ahead. But in this story רבי called such a document 'postdated', a document dated later than it was written, which means he did not know the custom. So how could he base an argument on it?

keyTerms.meaning: An expert; someone who knows a subject well
A tied document, a שטר מקושר, folded and stitched with witnesses signing on the back
A postdated document, dated later than the day it was really written

phrases.english: And was Rabbi an expert in tied documents?
But there was a certain tied document
that came before Rabbi,
and Rabbi said: This is a postdated document!
And Zunin said to Rabbi:
Such is the custom of this nation;
if he reigned one year, they count two for him,
if two, they count three for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the foundation of רבי's objection from step 1 and questions whether he could have made it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's objection in step 1, which assumed a שטר מקושר counts the king's years differently
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story shows רבי did not know the dating custom of tied documents, so he could not have built an objection on it.

steps.title: רבי learned the custom from זונין
steps.stepSummary: After hearing the custom from זונין, רבי accepted it, and only then did he make his objection.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he heard it from זונין, he accepted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story happened first. רבי learned the custom from זונין, agreed with it, and afterward used it in his objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction, because the two events happened at different times. The story with זונין came first, and רבי's objection to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל came after he already knew the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted it and held that way

phrases.english: After he heard it from Zunin, he held it.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי really did know the dating custom of a שטר מקושר. He learned it from זונין, so his objection in step 1 still stands.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing: the story came before the objection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי never knew the custom, so his objection had no basis
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי learned the custom from זונין and then relied on it

steps.title: A document dated 'in the year of so-and-so ארכן'
steps.stepSummary: A document gave its date only as 'the year of so-and-so ארכן'. רבי חנינא rules that we check when that ruler took office.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a document on which was written: 'In the year of so-and-so, ארכן.' רבי חנינא said: Let them check when this ארכן started his rule as ארכן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new case about a document dated by a ruler's title, without a year number. רבי חנינא says to find out when that ruler began his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The document gave no year count, only the ruler's name and the title ארכן. רבי חנינא treats this as the year the ruler took office, so finding that year tells us the document's date.

keyTerms.meaning: Archon, a title for a ruler or official
So-and-so, a stand-in for a name
His position as ארכן, his rule

phrases.english: There was a certain document on which was written:
'In the year of so-and-so, Archon.'
Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Let it be checked when the Archon rose to his position as archon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case about dating documents, linked to the earlier topic of counting a king's years.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A document dated 'the year of so-and-so ארכן' is dated to the year that ruler took office.

steps.title: Maybe the word means 'his reign was long'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests ארכן might not be a first-year title. It might mean the ruler's reign had already lasted a long time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it means that his rule had already gone on for a long time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי חנינא. Maybe the word does not point to the year the ruler began his rule at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ארכן sounds like the Aramaic אריך, 'long' or 'extended'. If it means 'his reign was long', the document could come from any later year, and checking when he took office would not tell us the date.

keyTerms.meaning: That it was long or extended

phrases.english: But perhaps it means that his reign had extended!
phrases.notes: The challenge is playing on how ארכן sounds like אריך, 'long'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חנינא's reading of the word ארכן in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's ruling that ארכן points to the year the ruler took office
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ארכן means 'his reign was long', the date could be any later year, so checking the start of his rule does not help.

steps.title: In that nation, ארכן is the title for the first year only
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא explains that this nation calls a ruler ארכן in his first year and דיגון in his second, so the document is from his first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: That is the custom of this nation. In the first year they call him 'ארכן'. In the second year they call him דיגון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא answers the challenge by explaining what the title ארכן means in that place. This supports רבי חנינא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ארכן is not a word meaning 'long'. It is a title that this nation uses only in the ruler's first year, and later years have a different title. So 'the year of so-and-so ארכן' must mean his first year, and checking when he took office gives the exact date.

keyTerms.meaning: A title used for a ruler in his second year

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:
Such is the custom of this nation;
in the first year they call him 'Archon,'
in the second year they call him Digon.

steps.whatToRemember: A document dated 'the year of so-and-so ארכן' means the ruler's first year, because in that nation ארכן is the first-year title. So רבי חנינא is right: check when he took office.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא כָּךְ מִנְהָגָהּ שֶׁל אוּמָּה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8 and supports רבי חנינא in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ארכן might mean 'his reign was long', so the year cannot be known
steps.terutzMaskana: ארכן is the title used only in a ruler's first year, so the document is from that year

steps.title: Maybe the ruler was removed and then put back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הושעיא's answer. Perhaps the ruler was thrown out and later put back, so 'ארכן' could mean the first year of his second term.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they removed him from power and then put him back again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that 'ארכן' must mean the ruler's very first year in office. A ruler who was removed and then brought back would also be in a 'first year', just of his second term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הושעיא taught that ארכן means first year and דיגון means second year. But if a ruler was removed and reinstated, a new 'first year' could start again later. Then the date on the שטר would still be unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: And then they put him back in power

phrases.english: But perhaps they removed him from office,
and then reinstated him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הושעיא's explanation from step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a document dated 'ארכן' must be from the ruler's first year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reinstated ruler could have a second 'first year', so the date is still not clear

steps.title: A reinstated ruler gets a different title
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that a ruler who was put back in power would be called 'ארכן דיגון', not just 'ארכן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Such a ruler would be called 'ארכן דיגון' (a second-time ruler).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge. A reinstated ruler has his own title, so a plain 'ארכן' can only mean the ruler's first term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this nation would add 'דיגון' (second) to the title of a reinstated ruler, a document that says just 'ארכן' cannot be talking about his second term. So we are back to רבי חנינא's ruling: check when he first took office.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'second-time ruler', the title for a ruler who was put back in power

steps.whatToRemember: A plain 'ארכן' on a שטר means the ruler's first year of his first term. A reinstated ruler would be called 'ארכן דיגון'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
That one, they would call him 'Archon Digon'.
phrases.notes: דיגון is Greek for 'two', so the title means 'second-time ruler'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: הָהוּא ״אַרְכָן דִּיגוֹן״ קָרְאוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification about how the nation names its rulers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A reinstated ruler might also be called plain 'ארכן', so the date would be unclear
steps.terutzMaskana: A reinstated ruler is called 'ארכן דיגון', so plain 'ארכן' means his first term

steps.title: A נזיר vow using Greek number-words
steps.stepSummary: Because the word דיגון came up, the גמרא brings a ברייתא. In it, סומכוס rules that a נזיר vow with the words הינא, דיגון, טריגון, טטריגון or פנטיגון means one, two, three, four or five terms of נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If someone says 'I am a נזיר הינא', סומכוס says: הינא means one term, דיגון two, טריגון three, טטריגון four, and פנטיגון five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related topic. It quotes a ברייתא that uses the same Greek number-words, here in the laws of נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each Greek word is a number, and סומכוס reads the vow by that number. A person who adds one of these words takes on that many terms of נזירות. This shows that דיגון really does mean 'two', as in 'ארכן דיגון'.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who vows to stay away from wine, haircuts and contact with the dead
A תנא, a student of רבי מאיר

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'I am hereby a nazirite heina' –
Sumakhos said: 'heina' means one term.
'Digon' means two; 'terigon' means three.
'Tetrigon' means four; 'pentigon' means five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא because the word דיגון came up
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a נזיר vow, הינא, דיגון, טריגון, טטריגון and פנטיגון mean one to five terms of נזירות

steps.title: Only a four-sided house can get נגעים
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא with the same words rules that a round, two-sided, three-sided or five-sided house cannot become טמא with נגעים. Only a four-sided house can.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A round house, or one with two, three or five sides, does not become טמא with נגעים. A four-sided house does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that uses these Greek shape-words, this time in the laws of נגעי בתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the words describe the shape of a house. A house is still a house whatever its shape, but the טומאה of נגעים only applies when it has exactly four sides. The גמרא will next ask where this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Can become טמא through צרעת spots

steps.confusionAlert: Here דיגון does not mean 'two years' or 'two terms'. It describes a house with two walls, one straight and one curved.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A round house, or a two-sided, three-sided or five-sided house –
phrases.notes: A two-sided house would have one straight wall and one curved wall.

phrases.english: does not become impure with leprous spots.
A four-sided house does become impure with leprous spots.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second related ברייתא using the same Greek words
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a four-sided house can become טמא with נגעים

steps.title: Where do we learn the four-wall rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that only a four-sided house can get נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the last ברייתא. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule with no reason. The גמרא wants to know which words in the Torah teach that a house needs four walls.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that a house needs four walls to get נגעים

steps.title: Two plural 'walls' make four
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers that the Torah says 'walls' (plural) twice. Each plural means at least two walls, so together they make four.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: Above, the Torah says 'walls' instead of 'wall', which means two. Below, it again says 'walls' instead of 'wall', another two. That makes four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that reads two פסוקים about נגעי בתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים say קירת (walls) where they could have said קיר (wall). Each plural counts as two walls. Two plus two makes four, so the house must have four walls.

keyTerms.meaning: Above / below: the earlier פסוק and the later פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Only a four-walled house can become טמא with נגעים. The Torah says 'walls' twice, and each time it means two walls.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
Above it says 'walls' and not 'wall', which means two;
below it says 'walls' and not 'wall', another two;
So there are four here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two plural 'walls' in ויקרא 14:37 and 14:39 add up to four walls

steps.title: A tied document seems to have no date
steps.stepSummary: A מקושר document comes before רבי. He thinks it has no date, but his son suggests the date is hidden in the folds, and it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain tied document came before רבי, and רבי said: Is there no date on this?! רבי שמעון the son of רבי said to him: Maybe the date is hidden between its knots? He opened it and saw it there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about a folded-and-tied document. רבי thinks it has no date until his son shows him the date is tucked inside the folds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the background for the next step. The story is not really about the date. It sets up רבי's displeasure with the document and his son's answer about who wrote it.

keyTerms.meaning: The date written on a document

phrases.english: A certain tied document
that came before Rabbi,
and Rabbi said: There is no date on this?!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי לְרַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, said to Rabbi:
Perhaps it is hidden between its knots?
He opened it and saw it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, moving away from the topic of houses with four walls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story: the date of a tied document was found hidden in its folds.

steps.title: Blaming the writer is called לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: רבי looks at his son with disapproval. The son says רבי יהודה חייטא wrote it, and רבי tells him to stay away from this לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Afterward רבי looked at him unhappily. He said: I did not write it, רבי יהודה the tailor wrote it. רבי said to him: Turn away from this לשון הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי is unhappy about the tied document. His son defends himself by naming the real writer, and רבי scolds him for speaking לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'someone else did it' when the thing was disliked puts that person in a bad light. That is why רבי calls it לשון הרע, even though the son was only defending himself.

keyTerms.meaning: With a bad or unhappy look

phrases.english: Afterward, Rabbi looked at him disapprovingly.
He said to him: I did not write it;
Rabbi Yehuda the tailor wrote it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּלָךְ מִלָּשׁוֹן הָרָע הַזֶּה.
phrases.english: He said to him: Turn away from this malicious speech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first story and gives its lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Naming someone as the writer of a disliked document is לשון הרע.

steps.title: Naming the writer of a praised ספר תהלים is also called לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: רבי praises the neat writing in a ספר תהלים. His son says יהודה חייטא wrote it, and רבי again calls it לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time, the son was sitting before רבי and reading a section of ספר תהלים. רבי said: How straight this writing is! He said: I did not write it, יהודה the tailor wrote it. רבי said: Turn away from this לשון הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: In a second story, רבי praises the writing and his son names the writer. Surprisingly, רבי calls this לשון הרע too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time nothing bad was said. The writer was being praised, so it is strange that רבי calls it לשון הרע. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.

phrases.english: Another time he was sitting before him,
and was reciting a section in the book of Psalms;

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: כַּמָּה מְיוּשָּׁר כְּתָב זֶה!
phrases.english: Rabbi said: How straight this writing is!
He said to him: I did not write it;
Yehuda the tailor wrote it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּלָךְ מִלָּשׁוֹן הָרָע הַזֶּה.
phrases.english: He said to him: Turn away from this malicious speech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story that ends the same way as the first, but here the writer is being praised.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even naming the writer of praised work is called לשון הרע.

steps.title: Why is praise considered לשון הרע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the first story involved לשון הרע, but asks what לשון הרע there is in the second story.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, there, in the first story, there is לשון הרע. But here, what לשון הרע is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second story. In the first story the writer was linked to something bad, but in the second he was only praised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'בשלמא... אלא' pattern accepts one case and attacks the other. The problem is that praise does not seem to fit the idea of negative speech.

phrases.english: Granted, there,
there is malicious speech;
but here,
what malicious speech is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the lesson of the second story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי calling the naming of a praised writer לשון הרע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Praise is not negative, so it should not count as לשון הרע.

steps.title: Praise can lead to criticism
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from רב דימי: never praise another person, because the praise can lead people to speak about his faults.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of רב דימי, the brother of רב ספרא, who taught: A person should never talk about the good qualities of his friend, because from talking about his good, he comes to talk about his bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that praise can also be a problem. Talking up someone's good points can lead to talking about his bad points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one person praises someone, a listener may answer, 'Yes, but...' and bring up his faults. So even praise can open the door to לשון הרע, which explains the second story.
steps.whatToRemember: Even praising someone can be a form of לשון הרע, because praise can lead others to bring up his faults.

phrases.english: Because of Rav Dimi,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנֵי רַב דִּימִי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סָפְרָא:
phrases.english: as Rav Dimi, the brother of Rav Safra, taught:
A person should never speak
of the good qualities of his friend,
for out of his praise one comes to his faults.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the second story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a teaching that widens the idea of לשון הרע
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only negative speech is לשון הרע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Praise can also lead to לשון הרע, so it should be avoided.

steps.title: Three sins no one escapes each day
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם quotes רב: every day a person fails in three things, which are sinful thoughts, עיון תפלה, and לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said in the name of רב: There are three sins that a person is not saved from every day: sinful thoughts, עיון תפלה, and לשון הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic of לשון הרע came up, the גמרא brings רב's teaching that lists it among three sins people stumble in daily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new teaching linked to the previous one by the subject of לשון הרע. It claims that some sins are so common that almost no one avoids them on any given day.

phrases.english: Rav Amram said that Rav said:
Three sins

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם נִיצּוֹל מֵהֶן בְּכׇל יוֹם –
phrases.english: a person is not saved from them every day:
sinful thoughts,
and 'looking into' prayer,
and malicious speech.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם אָמַר רַב שָׁלֹשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching brought because the topic of לשון הרע came up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No one escapes sinful thoughts, עיון תפלה, and לשון הרע every day.

steps.title: Does everyone really speak לשון הרע every day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that רב would say that no one avoids לשון הרע every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: לשון הרע? Could that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the third item on רב's list. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real לשון הרע is a serious sin that a person can avoid. So the claim that everyone commits it daily seems impossible, and the גמרא will need to explain what רב meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (an expression of surprise)

phrases.english: Malicious speech, can that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the third item in רב's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that no one avoids לשון הרע daily
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לשון הרע is a serious sin that people can avoid, so it cannot be something everyone does every day.
